stages.title: Scope / Authority Inventory
stages.objective: Resolve the final product checkpoint, full configured Module scope, canonical authority, and actual integrated Figma surfaces before judging quality.

stages.title: Product Semantics / Ownership Review
stages.objective: Review product semantics, capability consistency, Module ownership, and cross-Module responsibility boundaries against canonical authority.

stages.title: Journey / Cross-Module Review
stages.objective: Review complete Public/Admin journeys, backtracking, failure/recovery, and documented cross-Module handoffs rather than isolated frames.

stages.title: State / Responsive / Structural Review
stages.objective: Review required state observability, responsive continuity, canonical structure, composition, hierarchy, and applicable product-level design gates.

stages.title: False-Positive Challenge
stages.objective: Challenge every candidate blocking finding for authority trace, fresh artifact evidence, material product impact, scope validity, semantic identity, and tooling-vs-product distinction before authorizing repair.

stages.title: Bounded Product QA Repair
stages.objective: When a validated repairable QA gap exists, repair only the existing canonical Figma representations supported by product/design authority; never invent missing semantics or broaden product scope.

stages.title: Fresh Independent Product Review
stages.objective: Run a fresh independent review after repair; prior blocking observations are stale until re-observed. Continue the bounded review/repair loop until verified or a terminal blocker/budget exhaustion occurs.

stages.title: Product QA Handoff
stages.objective: Persist final Product QA status, mutation evidence, fresh verification evidence, and any terminal authority/target/budget blocker without creating a second canonical product specification.
